record.paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
record.context_brief: Admissible superpartitions and superconformal field theory
record.original_question: Determine the connection between admissible superpartitions and superconformal field theory: specifically, explain how the basis of states for the irreducible Neveu–Schwarz modules in the minimal superconformal model M(2,4p) is related to admissible superpartitions and the corresponding admissible Jack superpolynomials.

evidence.quote: Therefore, the ideal I^(k,r)_N defines a module over a subalgebra of the centerless Neveu-Schwarz algebra (i.e. the super-Virasoro algebra)

Open problem 3.4 – Connection with superconformal field theory. The basis of states for the irreducible Neveu-Schwarz modules in minimal superconformal model M(2, 4p) can be characterized by admissible superpartitions [34].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the algebra of symmetric polynomials in $N$ commuting variables $x_1,\dots,x_N$ and $N$ anticommuting (Grassmann) variables $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N$, invariant under the diagonal action of the symmetric group $S_N$. A superpartition $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$ is a pair consisting of a strictly decreasing partition $\Lambda^a=(\Lambda_1>\Lambda_2>\cdots>\Lambda_m\ge 0)$ (the fermionic part, of fermionic degree $m$) and a partition $\Lambda^s$ (the bosonic part). For positive integers $k,r$ with $\gcd(k+1,r-1)$ appropriate, a superpartition $\Lambda$ of length $\ell(\Lambda)\le N$ is called $(k,r,N)$-admissible if it satisfies the staircase-style separation condition
$$\Lambda_i-\Lambda_{i+k}\ge r\quad\text{whenever the corresponding parts are bosonic, with the analogous strict version for fermionic parts},$$
together with a tail condition on $\Lambda_{N-k+1},\dots,\Lambda_N$.

Jack superpolynomials $\mathcal{P}^{(\alpha)}_{\Lambda}(x;\theta)$ are the unique eigenfunctions of the supersymmetric trigonometric Calogero–Moser–Sutherland Hamiltonian which decompose triangularly (with respect to a fixed dominance order on superpartitions) on the monomial superfunctions $m_\Lambda$, normalized so that the coefficient of $m_\Lambda$ equals $1$. At the special value
$$\alpha=-\frac{k+1}{r-1},$$
let $I^{(k,r)}_N$ denote the linear span of the Jack superpolynomials $\mathcal{P}^{(\alpha)}_{\Lambda}$ indexed by $(k,r,N)$-admissible superpartitions $\Lambda$.

For $r=2$ and $k=2p-1$ (so that $\alpha=-2p/(2p-2)$ in the relevant minimal-model parametrization), consider the $N=1$ superconformal minimal model $M(2,4p)$ in the Neveu–Schwarz sector, with central charge $c=\tfrac{3}{2}\bigl(1-\tfrac{2(4p-2)^2}{8p}\bigr)$ and irreducible NS highest-weight modules $L_{r',s'}$ for the admissible Kac labels.

Problem. Establish a precise bijection between:
(i) the $(k,r,N)$-admissible superpartitions described above, and
(ii) a basis of states (e.g.\ a quasi-particle / Feigin–Stoyanovsky type basis) of the irreducible Neveu–Schwarz modules of the minimal superconformal model $M(2,4p)$,
in such a way that the corresponding admissible Jack superpolynomials $\mathcal{P}^{(\alpha)}_{\Lambda}$ at $\alpha=-(k+1)/(r-1)$ realize, in the large-$N$ limit, the basis vectors of these modules. In particular, prove that $I^{(k,r)}_N$ carries a module structure for (a suitable subalgebra of) the centerless Neveu–Schwarz (super-Virasoro) algebra and identify the resulting module with the appropriate direct sum of irreducible NS modules of $M(2,4p)$.
artifact.category_tag: Jack superpolynomials and superconformal minimal models
artifact.status_search_result: The connection between admissible superpartitions, Jack superpolynomials at negative rational parameter, and the Neveu–Schwarz sector of N=1 superconformal minimal models has been substantially developed: Blondeau-Fournier, Mathieu, Ridout and Wood ("Superconformal minimal models and admissible Jack polynomials", 2016) prove rationality and classify NS and Ramond modules in this framework, and earlier works construct super-Virasoro singular vectors via Jack superpolynomials. A complete, fully proven correspondence between the admissible-superpartition basis of $I^{(k,r)}_N$ and a basis of states of all irreducible NS modules of $M(2,4p)$ in the form requested appears to be partially established rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Superconformal minimal models and admissible Jack polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Rationality of N=1 superconformal minimal model VOSAs and classification of their NS and Ramond modules, with Jack polynomials at negative parameter indexed by admissible partitions describing free-fermion correlators.
status_evidence.claim: Major progress on the admissible-Jack/superconformal minimal model correspondence.

status_evidence.title: Ramond singular vectors and Jack superpolynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Super-Virasoro singular vectors expressed via differential operators acting on Jack superpolynomials indexed by superpartitions tied to (r,s).
status_evidence.claim: Singular-vector side of the correspondence is established.

status_evidence.title: Jack superpolynomials, superpartition ordering and determinantal formulas
status_evidence.snippet: Defines Jack superpolynomials and superpartition combinatorics underlying the conjectured connection.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the combinatorial framework on which the open problem is posed.
